newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PARIS ST GERMAIN LOSE DEFENSIVE RECORD BUT STAY TOP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARIS ST GERMAIN LOSE DEFENSIVE RECORD BUT STAY TOP.

text.p: Paris St Germain's Brazilian Brazilian coach Ricardo did not mince his words after his side conceded their first goals of the season on Saturday.
"We were appalling for half an hour. That first half hour, we must throw it away and forget it," said Ricardo after PSG fought back from 0-2 down to draw 2-2 at Guincamp.

PSG's unbeaten record was preserved because Ricardo's compatriots Rai and Leonardo saved their side with a 25th minute penalty and a 64th minute free kick respetively and that was enough to earn PSG a point and keep them unbeaten in nine matches and three points clear of Bastia at the top of the table.
The goals were the first they had conceded in any league or cup match this season.
"In the second half, you saw the real PSG, we didn't lose our nerve otherwise we could not have come back to 2-2" said Ricardo.
"After the two goals, I asked myself questions. But I managed to forget it," said young keeper Vincent Fernandez, who replaced injured international Bernard Lama last week.
Guingamp's Stephane Carnot scored the first goal against PSG this season in the ninth minute with Lionel Rouxel adding the second in the 15th.
Carnot's goal was the first conceded by PSG in a competitive match since May 18 when PSG beat Bastia 5-1, a total of 1,270 minues or just over 21 hours.
Lama, who did not play against Guincamp, has not conceded a goal in 1,169 minutes.
